field_basis.quantity_step: DERIVED — rule quoted, derivation shown. tick-and-lot-size-api.html: "Sizes are rounded to the szDecimals of that asset. For example, if szDecimals = 3 then 1.001 is a valid size but 1.0001 is not." BTC szDecimals=5 (frozen api-info-meta.json). A size is valid iff it has at most szDecimals decimal places, so the smallest positive increment between two valid sizes is 10^-szDecimals = 10^-5 = 0.00001 BTC.
field_basis.price_tick: RULE-DERIVED, NON-SCALAR — no single tick value is printed for BTC. tick-and-lot-size-api.html: "Prices can have up to 5 significant figures, but no more than MAX_DECIMALS - szDecimals decimal places where MAX_DECIMALS is 6 for perps and 8 for spot. Integer prices are always allowed, regardless of the number of significant figures." BTC szDecimals=5, perp MAX_DECIMALS=6 => at most 6-5=1 decimal place, i.e. price granularity floor 10^-1 = 0.1. The 5-significant-figure cap makes the effective increment coarser at BTC price magnitudes: a price in [100000, 999990] has 5 significant figures at a 10 increment; a price in [10000, 99999] resolves to integer (1) since 12345.6 already exceeds 5 significant figures. Because the venue defines price validity by a rule (sig figs + decimal bound + integers-always-allowed) rather than a published per-asset scalar, price_tick remains null and the rule is carried verbatim in additional_venue_metadata.price_rule.
field_basis.minimum_quantity: GAP — not literally stated in the frozen sources. The frozen minimums are notional, not quantity: order-types.html "$100 minimum total order size" (TWAP only) and error-responses.html "Order must have minimum value of $10." (MinTradeNtl). A notional minimum is not a quantity minimum and is not converted to BTC here. Lower bound only: the smallest representable non-zero BTC size equals quantity_step = 0.00001 BTC; no minimum quantity is inferred.
field_basis.minimum_notional: FILLED v1.3 — QUOTED, with source-context caveat. error-responses.html (fifth fetch) is the venue's batched order/cancel error catalogue; the row Error source = "Order", Error type = "MinTradeNtl", Error string = "Order must have minimum value of $10." gives the perp minimum order notional. Recorded as 10 (venue prints "$10"; the instrument settles in USDC and the contract-spec page applies no USDC/USDT conversion). SOURCE CONTEXT: this is an API error-response document ("Below is a list of possible batched error responses"), NOT a contract-specification table — it is the reject threshold the matching engine enforces, not a figure published in a spec table. The separate row "MinTradeSpotNtl" ("Order must have minimum value of 10 {quote_token}.") is the spot-market variant and does not apply to this LINEAR_PERPETUAL record. The earlier TWAP-only "$100 minimum total order size" from order-types.html is unchanged and stays in additional_venue_metadata.twap_minimum_total_order_size.
field_basis.point_value: FILLED v1.2 — DERIVED definitional identity. contract-specifications.html states "Instrument type" = "Linear perpetual", "Contract" = "1 unit of underlying spot asset", and "USDT pnl is denominated in USDC" with no USDC/USDT conversion applied. For one contract, a 1.0 price-unit move therefore changes numerical PnL by 1.0 USDC: point_value = 1 USDC per 1.0 price unit per contract.

size_rule.quoted_text: Sizes are rounded to the szDecimals of that asset. For example, if szDecimals = 3 then 1.001 is a valid size but 1.0001 is not. szDecimals for an asset is found in the meta response to the info endpoint

price_rule.quoted_text: Prices can have up to 5 significant figures, but no more than MAX_DECIMALS - szDecimals decimal places where MAX_DECIMALS is 6 for perps and 8 for spot. Integer prices are always allowed, regardless of the number of significant figures. E.g. 123456 is a valid price even though 12345.6 is not.
price_rule.perp_price_examples_quoted: 1234.5 is valid but 1234.56 is not (too many significant figures). 0.001234 is valid, but 0.0012345 is not (more than 6 decimal places). If szDecimals = 1 , 0.01234 is valid but 0.012345 is not (more than 6 - szDecimals decimal places)

point_value_definition.unit: USDC per 1.0 price unit per contract
quoted_text: Note that no conversions with the USDC/USDT exchange rate are applied, so these contracts are technically quanto contracts where USDT pnl is denominated in USDC.
